ministry_ne: भूमि व्यवस्था, सहकारी, सङ्‍घीय मामिला तथा सामान्य प्रशासन मन्त्रालय
summary:
The main purpose of the Federal Civil Service Act, 2083 is to make provisions regarding the constitution, operation, and conditions of service of the federal civil service, and to develop it as a governance-oriented mechanism committed to the national interest and federal democratic republic, politically neutral, professionally competent, inclusive, and professional (Explanatory Note, Page xi). This Act shall come into force immediately upon certification (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 1).

The Ministry handling general administration matters shall act as the central body regarding the constitution, operation, and management of civil servants of the federal civil service (Section 3, Subsection 1, Page 2). The basic principles of the federal civil service must also be adopted in the provincial civil service, local service, and all other government services (Section 4, Subsection 2, Page 2). A provincial civil service and one local service shall remain in each province, which shall be governed by provincial law subject to the standards specified in this Act (Explanatory Note, Page xxxv, xxxvi). The post of Chief Secretary of the provincial government shall be a post of the federal civil service, and Nepal Government shall assign an officer from among the 13th level employees of the federal civil service (Explanatory Note, Page xxxv). Until a 12th level employee is appointed in the provincial service, Nepal Government shall assign an employee of the federal civil service who is at the 12th level or has completed a service period of at least five years at the 11th level to act as the secretary of a provincial ministry (Explanatory Note, Page xxxv). Until employees are appointed at all local levels, Nepal Government may assign federal civil service employees to act as chief administrative officers (Explanatory Note, Page xxxvi). The salary and other benefits of employees adjusted or deputed to the provincial civil service or local service shall be provided by the respective province or local level (Explanatory Note, Page xxxvi).

This bill provides for a Civil Service Board to supervise and regulate the transfer, placement, and career management of civil servants up to Gazetted Second Class to make such activities accountable, transparent, and merit-based, with the Chief Secretary of Nepal Government as its chairperson (Explanatory Note, Page xvii). The chief executive of the board is not stated in the bill. Nepal Government may establish an Employee Welfare Fund for the welfare of serving employees, retired employees, and their family members of the federal civil service (Explanatory Note, Page xxxix).

Under the bill, reprimand shall be given for evading responsibility, being absent more than two times in a month without prior approval, failing to receive transfer clearance or hand over charge, or consuming alcohol during office hours (Explanatory Note, Page xxx). Punishment of withholding up to five salary increments or withholding promotion for up to five years shall be imposed for failing to fulfill official duties responsibly, ignoring complaints of service seekers, or submitting false details in a promotion application (Explanatory Note, Page xxxi). An employee shall be removed from service without being disqualified for future government service for remaining absent for 30 consecutive days without written information or approved leave, or failing to report within 30 days after completing foreign study (Explanatory Note, Page xxxi, xxxii). An employee shall be dismissed from service with disqualification for future government service for involvement in political activities, being convicted by a court of corruption, forgery, or criminal charges involving moral turpitude, or obtaining foreign permanent residency (Explanatory Note, Page xxxii). Departmental punishment shall be imposed by Nepal Government for employees working in Gazetted First Class and above, by the Gazetted Special Class officer of the entity for Gazetted Second and Third Class, and by the Departmental Head or Gazetted Office Head for Non-Gazetted posts (Explanatory Note, Page xxxii, xxxiii). An appeal against a departmental punishment order may be made to the Administrative Court (Explanatory Note, Page xxxiv). The time limit for filing an appeal is not stated in the bill.

This bill repeals the Civil Service Act, 2049 and provides that actions taken under that Act shall be deemed to have been taken under this Act (Explanatory Note, Page xli). What happens to the staff, assets, and funds of the repealed Act is not stated in the bill.
title: Federal Civil Service Act, 2083
